      "source_quote": "The spectral characteristics of a typical four-layer structure using the transition metal Cr as the solar absorbing layer [SiO 2 (90nm)/Cr(10nm)/SiO 2 (80nm)/Al(100nm)] are in Fig. 5 to show that a very high optical absorption (>95%) over the wide wavelength range from 400nm to 1200nm can be achieved",

      "physical_effect": "High absorption in visible/NIR via interference and multiple reflections; high IR reflection from bottom Al.",
      "conditions_and_unknowns": [
        "Specific thicknesses (90/10/80 nm) are for a specific design point; optimal values for strict 400-700 vs 700-2000 split may differ.",
        "Source uses Al substrate but does not explicitly detail HfO2 substitution effects."
      ],
      "goal_ids": ["G1", "G2"],
      "inference_bridge": "Hypothesize that replacing SiO2 with HfO2 (higher index) or adjusting the dielectric thickness ratio can sharpen the transition between the absorption band (visible) and reflection band (NIR) to better match the task's specific cutoff at 700 nm."
    },

      "physical_effect": "Interference-enhanced absorption in visible; IR reflection by metal layers.",
      "conditions_and_unknowns": [
        "Text contains a likely error stating dielectrics absorb visible light (usually they are transparent spacers); we interpret this as dielectrics enabling absorption via interference in the metal.",
        "Does not specify HfO2/SiO2 combination specifically."
      ],
      "goal_ids": ["G1", "G2"],
      "inference_bridge": "Propose a multi-cavity stack using HfO2/SiO2 pairs with thin Cr interlayers to broaden the visible absorption bandwidth while maintaining NIR reflectance through the cumulative effect of multiple reflective interfaces."
    },
    {
      "id": "D3",
      "evidence_id": "E_6b64f066b82f4fe1ca46484b331c60d42edf94c5c362464423524ae0c80edbb1",

      "structure_or_method": "Substitution of SiO2 with HfO2 in anti-reflection or spacer layers.",
      "physical_effect": "Improved thermal stability and potentially altered optical impedance matching.",
      "conditions_and_unknowns": [
        "Context is high-temperature stability (800 C); optical benefit at room temperature for spectral selectivity is inferred but not explicitly quantified in the snippet.",

      "inference_bridge": "Utilize HfO2 as the primary high-index spacer instead of SiO2 to leverage its higher refractive index for stronger interference effects in fewer layers, potentially improving the sharpness of the visible/NIR transition."
